attempts.text: The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including a preoperative PSA of 6.9 and an ISUP grade group 2 pathology from the prostatectomy specimen. Positive findings include negative surgical margins and no seminal vesicle invasion or lymphovascular invasion documented. A countervailing finding is the absence of nodal sampling; thus, pNx status widens uncertainty regarding nodal involvement. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy comparison shows concordance in Gleason pattern (3+4/ISUP 2). Prognostic revision would be significantly aided by postoperative PSA levels and their subsequent trajectory. The current data lacks information on these critical follow-up markers.

The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including a preoperative PSA of 6.9 and an ISUP grade group of 2 from both biopsy and prostatectomy specimens. Positive prognostic indicators include negative surgical margins, no extraprostatic extension, and no seminal vesicle invasion documented in the pathology report. Conversely, the absence of nodal sampling widens uncertainty regarding regional spread, as no lymph nodes were removed. The lack of documentation regarding seminal vesicles or node status limits definitive staging information.

Information that would significantly revise this prognosis includes postoperative PSA levels and their subsequent trajectory; a rising or persistently elevated PSA warrants closer investigation. Furthermore, obtaining comprehensive nodal sampling would clarify the risk profile by assessing for occult metastases. Given the current data, the expected follow-up without an event is 76.7 months, with a heuristic sensitivity range of 49.9 to 103.5 months.
